title: What are Arrays?
overview: Arrays are data structures used to store multiple values in a single variable. Each value in an array has a position called an index.

title: Creating and Accessing Arrays
overview: Arrays can be created using square brackets. Values inside arrays can be accessed using their index number. Array indexes start from 0.

title: Adding and Removing Array Elements
overview: JavaScript provides methods like push, pop, shift, and unshift to add or remove elements from arrays.

example.title: Array Methods
example.content:
push(): Adds element at end
pop(): Removes last element
shift(): Removes first element
unshift(): Adds element at beginning

title: Array Length and Iteration
overview: The length property returns the number of elements in an array. Loops can be used to access each item inside an array.

example.title: Array Iteration

title: Array Methods
overview: JavaScript provides built-in array methods that help developers perform common operations like searching, modifying, and transforming data.

title: map and filter Methods
overview: map creates a new array by transforming each element, while filter creates a new array containing only elements that match a condition.

example.title: map and filter Example

title: Destructuring Arrays
overview: Array destructuring allows developers to extract values from arrays and store them directly into variables using a shorter syntax.

example.title: Destructuring Example

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how arrays store multiple values, access elements, modify arrays, use array methods, iterate through arrays, and use destructuring.
